name: Ed's Agentic Finance Rails
description: Agent access to brokerage accounts: one record per provider. Values are sourced or 'unknown'.

providers.summary: Alpaca's hosted Trading MCP uses OAuth for live and paper accounts; a local MCP and a CLI use API keys. No broker-side per-order approval is documented.
providers.auth: Hosted Trading MCP: OAuth sign-in with an Alpaca account (plugins for Cursor, Claude Code and Codex). Local Trading MCP and CLI: API key and secret in environment variables
providers.endpoint_note: Paper trading uses https://paper-api.alpaca.markets/mcp. The local server runs over stdio.
providers.notes: Earlier research could not confirm a hosted retail MCP; Alpaca's own agentic repo now documents one. The Broker API MCP (beta) is a separate B2B product for broker partners.

providers.summary: Coinbase for Agents: a remote MCP with OAuth for allowlisted clients, or a local CLI with an API key. Coinbase enforces trade limits, and a dedicated portfolio is optional.
providers.auth: OAuth via login.coinbase.com for the remote MCP; Dynamic Client Registration and Client ID Metadata Documents supported, but clients are allowlisted; the local CLI uses a CDP API key
providers.limits: Maximum trade size in USD, a 24-hour volume limit and an auto-stop after a set percentage loss, set in the Coinbase app or on the web and enforced by Coinbase. Amounts are chosen by each user
providers.notes: The dedicated portfolio is optional; the main account can also be used. Isolated agent portfolios are spot-crypto only. Per-order confirmation depends on the AI client and, in ChatGPT, on which Coinbase connection you use.

providers.summary: Remote MCP connector. By default the AI drafts trade instructions you review and submit; eligible accounts can enable Autonomous Trading in an AI Partition.
providers.auth: IBKR's own login and authorization flow; credentials are never shared with the AI app; revoke in Client Portal > Settings > Manage Third-Party Consents
providers.limits: Autonomous Trading: funding limited to cash allocated to the AI Partition; funding, account and eligibility limits apply at launch (amounts not published in the sources)
providers.endpoint_note: The Claude connector directory lists https://api.ibkr.com/v1/api/mcp for IBKR's certified connector.
providers.notes: can_place_orders and approval_model list the default AI Integration first, then Autonomous Trading. The exact asset list for Autonomous Trading is unclear; an independent review found IBKR's descriptions inconsistent.

providers.summary: Kraken ships a local MCP server with its CLI. It runs on your own machine, can trade live only when you turn on trading services, and asks you to approve each order, withdrawal or transfer.
providers.auth: API key and secret in environment variables, or a stored key: a browser sign-in key from kraken auth login (restricted, no withdrawal rights, expires after 90 days by default) or a key you created, stored with kraken setup
providers.limits: Position size limits and pair allowlists can be set on the API key in Kraken's settings
providers.endpoint_note: The MCP server, kraken-mcp, runs locally over stdio and is not exposed as a network service. There is no Kraken-hosted MCP endpoint.
providers.notes: Dangerous tools ask for approval on every call through MCP elicitation; a client that cannot show the prompt relies on its own tool-approval setting, and --allow-dangerous turns the gate off. The kraken CLI itself places orders without a confirmation prompt.

providers.summary: Public runs a hosted MCP server at mcp.public.com/mcp for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Meta Muse, Perplexity and Grok. Most apps sign in with OAuth; Muse uses a Public API key. Every trade is a real order, with no paper mode.
providers.auth: OAuth for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Perplexity and Grok; a Public API key as the bearer token for Meta Muse and for the Public Agent Skill
providers.limits: Hosted server: unknown. Self-hosted server release 0.11.0: optional per-order quantity and value limits set in environment variables, off by default
providers.notifications: Trade confirmations in real time, per Public's MCP page
providers.notes: approval_model lists the hosted server first (dedicated accounts are optional), then the self-hosted server from release 0.11.0, which asks you to confirm each order. Whether the hosted server confirms each order is unknown. The Claude directory connector cannot place trades; a custom connector can.

providers.summary: Remote Trading MCP with OAuth. Agents read all Robinhood accounts but trade only in a dedicated agentic (MCP) account; per-order approval is an optional toggle.
assets: crypto (not in some states, including New York)
providers.auth: OAuth to the remote MCP server; protected-resource metadata lists the scope "internal"; an independent test reports PKCE and dynamic client registration
providers.notifications: Push notification whenever the agent makes a trade, plus a real-time activity feed and P&L in the app
providers.notes: Trade approvals are off by default for MCP accounts. Robinhood's article said on 2026-11-12 that they were still rolling out; the 2026-11-19 version no longer says so. Built-in Robinhood Agents are a separate product.

providers.summary: Scalable Capital runs an MCP server with four access levels you set in its web app. Buy and sell orders need Full access, and each order needs your fresh, explicit confirmation of a preview.
providers.auth: Browser sign-in to Scalable through the AI app, with two-factor authentication; the MCP access level is set in the web version under Profile > Security > Agentic Investing
providers.notes: One access level applies to every connected AI assistant and every portfolio. Orders need the Full access level. The Scalable CLI's access setting is managed separately. Personal Broker, Overnight and Fixed-Term accounts are supported; Junior accounts are not.

providers.summary: Webull's hosted Cloud MCP prepares trades you confirm in the Webull app; its local OpenAPI MCP places orders directly, with risk limits and a sandbox default.
providers.auth: Cloud MCP: OAuth authorization code flow with a per-account Non-Trading or Trading capability. Local OpenAPI MCP: App Key and App Secret, with a 2FA flow
providers.limits: Local OpenAPI MCP only: per-market maximum order notional (default USD 10,000 for the US market), quantity limits and a symbol whitelist
providers.notes: can_place_orders and approval_model list the Cloud MCP first, then the local OpenAPI MCP. Paper trading refers to the local MCP's UAT sandbox; for Cloud MCP it is unknown.
